policy.purpose: Core (1A) is the difficulty-aware, prior-knowledge-aware subtopic-bucket teaching layer between source/Core (1) semantics and Core (2) transfer.
policy.primary_question_rule: Each Revised Core (2) v2 question belongs to exactly one primary SBA bucket; secondary prerequisites may be attached separately.
policy.production_selection_rule: For the current build queue, do not publish a dedicated SBA PDF when core2_primary_questions is empty; retain the bucket in the chapter map as SKIP_NO_PRIMARY_CORE2.
policy.priority_rule: Prioritise MEDIUM/HARD buckets for learners at or below 50% usable prior knowledge; increase visual staging, prerequisite rebuilding and worked-example guidance as readiness falls.
policy.core2_hint_preteach_rule: Every Core (2) H1/H2/H3 reveal must trace to an earlier Core (1A) learning atom and to an example/check; a question may be held until its release prerequisite buckets are complete.
policy.teaching_sequence_rule: Foundation/pretraining -> story/phenomenon -> staged picture -> what changed physically -> picture-to-maths bridge -> worked example -> guided/faded practice -> retrieval gate -> Core (2).

buckets.production_reason: Has one or more primary Revised Core (2) v2 questions; publish according to difficulty/readiness.

learning_atoms.title: A motion story can be described with or without the clock
learning_atoms.purpose: Distinguish the time-parametric description x(t), y(t) from the geometric path description y(x), so the learner knows why time elimination is useful.
teaching_moves: show the same projectile with time stamps
show the same curve with only x and y coordinates
ask what information remains if the clock labels are removed
name y(x) as a path relation, not a new force law
misconceptions: trajectory equation gives the time of flight
removing time changes the actual motion
checks: decide whether a question asks for state at a time or height at a horizontal position

learning_atoms.title: Write the two component equations before eliminating anything
learning_atoms.purpose: Rebuild x=u_x t and y=u_y t-1/2 gt^2 under the ordinary ideal projectile model and identify the shared time variable.
teaching_moves: state the coordinate frame and launch origin
write horizontal equation first
write vertical equation second
circle the same t in both equations
state a_x=0 and a_y=-g as model conditions
misconceptions: eliminate time before writing both component equations
use the trajectory shortcut when horizontal acceleration is not zero
checks: write x(t) and y(t) from a component diagram before any substitution

learning_atoms.title: Eliminate time one substitution at a time
learning_atoms.purpose: Derive the trajectory equation from the component equations without an algebra jump.
teaching_moves: solve x=u_x t for t=x/u_x
place that exact expression into y(t)
expand the square carefully
simplify to y=(u_y/u_x)x-gx^2/(2u_x^2)
translate u_y/u_x to tan(theta) and u_x to u cos(theta)
misconceptions: forget to square u_x in the gravity term
checks: derive the component form and angle form from the same starting equations

learning_atoms.title: Read the physics hidden in the trajectory equation
learning_atoms.purpose: Interpret the linear term as launch slope and the negative quadratic term as downward curvature, and connect the quadratic form with a parabola.
teaching_moves: separate the linear and quadratic terms visually
show that u_y/u_x is the launch slope
show that gravity contributes the negative x^2 term
compare g=0 with g>0 schematically
identify a downward-opening parabola
misconceptions: the x^2 term means horizontal acceleration
the trajectory equation creates a new law separate from component motion
checks: predict how increasing g or u_x changes the curvature without solving a full problem

learning_atoms.title: Read initial components directly from vector notation
learning_atoms.purpose: Teach that an initial velocity written as a i-hat + b j-hat already gives u_x=a and u_y=b, so unnecessary angle-finding can be avoided.
teaching_moves: draw i-hat along x and j-hat along y
map vector coefficients to horizontal and vertical components
substitute directly into the component-form trajectory equation
contrast direct component use with the longer angle route
misconceptions: i-hat and j-hat are units rather than directions
must calculate the launch angle before using the trajectory equation
checks: extract u_x and u_y from a symbolic a i-hat+b j-hat launch velocity

learning_atoms.title: A wall gives a horizontal coordinate event
learning_atoms.purpose: Connect a known x-location to the shared clock by finding time from horizontal motion, then determine y; also show the equivalent direct trajectory route.
teaching_moves: draw a vertical wall at x=x_w
route A: find t=x_w/u_x then use y(t)
route B: substitute x_w directly into y(x)
place both routes side by side
use the no-gravity rise as a reasonableness check
misconceptions: the wall coordinate is a flight time
use y=0 at the wall unless the wall happens to meet the launch level
checks: choose the time route or direct trajectory route for a known x-coordinate

learning_atoms.title: The range form exposes the two zero-height points
learning_atoms.purpose: Teach the source alternate form y=x(1-x/R)tan(theta) and interpret x=0 and x=R as the same-height launch and landing intersections.
teaching_moves: factor the trajectory relation using the same-height range R
show the x factor gives the launch point
show 1-x/R gives the landing point
connect the midpoint symmetry of the parabola without claiming every projectile is same-height
misconceptions: the range form is valid for unequal launch and landing heights
R is a universal x-intercept for every coordinate origin
checks: verify y=0 at x=0 and x=R and state the validity condition

learning_atoms.title: Check a trajectory equation before trusting it
learning_atoms.purpose: Build fast validity and sanity checks: origin, dimensions, sign of curvature, model conditions and agreement with component equations.
teaching_moves: check y(0)=0 for launch-origin coordinates
check the x coefficient is dimensionless
check the x^2 coefficient has units of inverse length
check the quadratic coefficient is negative under downward gravity
state that added horizontal acceleration changes the derivation
misconceptions: a memorised formula is safe without checking its coordinate origin or model
any quadratic y(x) automatically represents this projectile model
checks: audit a candidate equation using origin, sign and units before calculation

hint_rungs.evidence: Known wall x-coordinate is taught as an event; horizontal motion gives the time to that x-position.
Both routes are taught: substitute the wall time into y(t), or evaluate the already-derived trajectory y(x).
Guided wall example begins with t=x_wall/u_x before any vertical calculation.
Coefficients of i-hat and j-hat are explicitly taught as the initial horizontal and vertical components.
The component-form trajectory y=(u_y/u_x)x-gx^2/(2u_x^2) is derived step by step before transfer.
Guided practice starts by identifying u_x and u_y directly from vector notation before substitution.
